summary:
Field Shift is a prototype agricultural decision-support website that helps users explore which crops may suit a location and compare possible crop-rotation strategies. Users select a place on a map and review environmental indicators—including weather, water availability, soil moisture, and terrain—in one view. The prototype flags missing data and presents potential crop matches and rotation options for further consideration.
The project addresses the challenge of fragmented environmental information, which can make agricultural planning harder as heat, rainfall, and water conditions change. By making relevant indicators easier to inspect and compare, Field Shift aims to help farmers and planners make more informed, location-aware decisions. It is an exploratory tool, not a substitute for local agronomic advice; its data connections and recommendations still require further validation.
details:
Field Shift is a bilingual, map-first web prototype for agricultural decision support. A user selects a location on an interactive map and reviews available environmental information—such as climate, rainfall, soil moisture, terrain and satellite-derived vegetation indicators—in a dashboard. The prototype includes source and data-quality cues, including flags for missing information, alongside two separate decision-support components: a crop-suitability classifier and a crop-rotation planner that can consider crop history and farming constraints.

The goal is to make scattered environmental indicators easier to explore together, helping farmers, researchers and planners ask better-informed questions before making decisions. The interface is designed for both Arabic and English users. Its creative approach is to pair a map-based workflow with transparent data limitations, while keeping crop matching distinct from rotation planning. The team considered local differences in soil and climate, changing water availability, data gaps and source coverage, prior crops and other farm constraints. The tool is intended to support—not replace—local agronomic expertise.

The project materials describe a Random Forest crop classifier evaluated on Crop_recommendation.csv, with a reported 99.32% test accuracy on that dataset. This is not evidence of global field accuracy or validation with NASA satellite data. The demo visibly shows NASA POWER metrics and a GIBS layer selector; other listed data connections and recommendations should not be assumed to be independently verified or live.
